newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey $600 mln CP TRANs F1-plus - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey $600 mln CP TRANs F1-plus - Fitch.

text.p: New Jersey's $600 million (commercial paper) tax and revenue anticipation notes, series Fiscal 1997A are rated 'F-1+' by Fitch Investors Service.
Although a maximum of $600 million may be issued, the initial amount is $550 million and currently the state does not plan to use the remaining $50 million.
The notes will be dated as of the date of delivery and final maturity is June 13, 1997. Liquidity will be furnished under an advance agreement with Union Bank of Switzerland, New York branch.
The commercial paper notes are special obligations of the state, payable solely from moneys on deposit in the general and property tax relief funds attributable to fiscal 1996 and legally available.

Appropriations, which have been made, are required for principal and interest; the notes are not general obligations. The notes are well protected, with the total principal amount of expected operating borrowing equal to about 2% of cash flow and 75% of principal and interest required to be set aside by May 31.
Coverage of the maximum authorization is a comfortable 3.1 times. The estimated closing balance leaves a good margin of safety, at 4% of cash receipts.
The revenue assumptions appear realistic and assumed growth matches experience to date. Employment has been growing since 1993, and in 1995 was only about 2% below the pre- recession peak.
